title: ECG Analysis: R-Peak Detection and HRV Pipeline
text: PhysioECG provides complete pipeline electrocardiogram (ECG) analysis built PhysioExperiment data model. vignette demonstrates core workflow: R-peak detection, RR interval computation, ectopic beat handling, heart rate variability (HRV) analysis across time-domain, frequency-domain, nonlinear methods.

title: ECG Analysis: R-Peak Detection and HRV Pipeline
code: library(PhysioECG) library(PhysioCore)

title: ECG Analysis: R-Peak Detection and HRV Pipeline
text: PhysioECG includes data generators creating synthetic ECG signals. make_ecg() function produces PhysioExperiment Gaussian-shaped R-peaks regular intervals. testing realistic noise, use make_ecg_noisy():
code: # Create a 10-second ECG recording at 500 Hz with heart rate of 72 bpm pe <- make_ecg(n_time = 5000, n_channels = 1, sr = 500, heart_rate = 72) pe pe_noisy <- make_ecg_noisy(   n_time = 5000, sr = 500, heart_rate = 72,   baseline_amp = 0.3, powerline_amp = 0.1, noise_sd = 0.15 )

title: ECG Analysis: R-Peak Detection and HRV Pipeline
text: analysis, assess signal quality identify channels poor recording conditions. R-peaks detected, passing ecgSignalQuality() enables QRS-based SNR estimation accurate quality metrics.
code: # Assess signal quality without peak information sq <- ecgSignalQuality(pe) sq peaks <- ecgDetectRpeaks(pe) sq <- ecgSignalQuality(pe, peaks = peaks) sq

title: ECG Analysis: R-Peak Detection and HRV Pipeline
text: Remove low-frequency baseline wander R-peak detection best results.
code: # High-pass moving-average subtraction (default) pe_clean <- ecgBaselineCorrect(pe_noisy, method = "highpass", cutoff = 0.5)  # Alternatively, use running median subtraction pe_clean2 <- ecgBaselineCorrect(pe_noisy, method = "median", cutoff = 0.5)

title: ECG Analysis: R-Peak Detection and HRV Pipeline
text: ecgDetectRpeaks() function implements Pan-Tompkins algorithm adaptive dual-threshold classification. automatically handles inverted ECG signals. result data.frame columns channel, sample, time_sec, amplitude detected R-peak.
code: peaks <- ecgDetectRpeaks(pe, method = "pan_tompkins") head(peaks)

title: ECG Analysis: R-Peak Detection and HRV Pipeline
text: noisy signals unusual heart rates, tune detection parameters:
code: # Lower threshold for weak signals; increase refractory for slow heart rates peaks <- ecgDetectRpeaks(   pe,   threshold_factor = 0.4,   refractory_ms = 250 )

title: ECG Analysis: R-Peak Detection and HRV Pipeline
text: Compute RR intervals detected R-peaks. resulting data.frame standard input HRV analysis functions.
code: rr <- ecgRRintervals(pe, peaks) head(rr)

title: ECG Analysis: R-Peak Detection and HRV Pipeline
text: HRV analysis, identify correct ectopic (abnormal) beats can bias HRV metrics. Correct ectopic beats interpolation removal:
code: # Detect ectopic beats using local median comparison rr_checked <- ecgQualityCheck(rr, threshold_ms = 300) table(rr_checked$is_ectopic) # Linear interpolation (default) -- preserves series length rr_corrected <- ecgRRcorrect(rr_checked, method = "interpolate")  # Or remove ectopic beats entirely rr_removed <- ecgRRcorrect(rr_checked, method = "remove")

title: ECG Analysis: R-Peak Detection and HRV Pipeline
text: Compute standard time-domain HRV metrics: SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50, mean RR, mean heart rate. Task Force European Society Cardiology (1996) recommends minimum recording length 5 minutes short-term HRV analysis.
code: hrv_time <- ecgHRVtime(rr_corrected) hrv_time

title: ECG Analysis: R-Peak Detection and HRV Pipeline
text: Compute frequency-domain HRV metrics using Welch’s method Lomb-Scargle periodogram: Standard frequency bands VLF (0.003–0.04 Hz), LF (0.04–0.15 Hz), HF (0.15–0.4 Hz). Custom bands can specified:
code: # Welch's method (resamples to uniform 4 Hz grid) hrv_freq <- ecgHRVfreq(rr_corrected, method = "welch") hrv_freq # Lomb-Scargle periodogram (handles uneven sampling directly) hrv_freq_ls <- ecgHRVfreq(rr_corrected, method = "lomb") hrv_freq_ls hrv_freq_custom <- ecgHRVfreq(   rr_corrected,   vlf_band = c(0.003, 0.04),   lf_band = c(0.04, 0.15),   hf_band = c(0.15, 0.5) )

title: ECG Analysis: R-Peak Detection and HRV Pipeline
text: Compute nonlinear HRV metrics including Poincare plot descriptors (SD1, SD2), sample entropy, detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA).

title: ECG Analysis: R-Peak Detection and HRV Pipeline
code: # Poincare plot descriptors poincare <- ecgHRVpoincare(rr_corrected) poincare  # Sample entropy sampen <- ecgSampleEntropy(rr_corrected, m = 2, r_factor = 0.2) sampen  # Detrended fluctuation analysis dfa <- ecgDFA(rr_corrected, short_range = c(4, 16), long_range = c(16, 64)) dfa

title: ECG Analysis: R-Peak Detection and HRV Pipeline
text: Use ecgHRVnonlinear() compute nonlinear metrics :
code: hrv_nl <- ecgHRVnonlinear(rr_corrected) hrv_nl

title: ECG Analysis: R-Peak Detection and HRV Pipeline
text: full pipeline raw ECG HRV metrics:
code: # 1. Load or simulate ECG data pe <- make_ecg(n_time = 60000, n_channels = 1, sr = 500, heart_rate = 68)  # 2. Assess signal quality sq <- ecgSignalQuality(pe)  # 3. Correct baseline wander pe <- ecgBaselineCorrect(pe, method = "highpass", cutoff = 0.5,                          output_assay = "clean")  # 4. Detect R-peaks on cleaned signal peaks <- ecgDetectRpeaks(pe, assay_name = "clean")  # 5. Compute RR intervals rr <- ecgRRintervals(pe, peaks)  # 6. Detect and correct ectopic beats rr <- ecgQualityCheck(rr, threshold_ms = 300) rr <- ecgRRcorrect(rr, method = "interpolate")  # 7. Compute HRV metrics hrv_time <- ecgHRVtime(rr) hrv_freq <- ecgHRVfreq(rr, method = "welch") hrv_nl <- ecgHRVnonlinear(rr)  # 8. Combine results list(   time_domain = hrv_time,   freq_domain = hrv_freq,   nonlinear = hrv_nl )

title: ECG Morphology: PQRST Segmentation and Interval Analysis
text: Beyond heart rate HRV analysis, morphology individual ECG waveforms carries important clinical research information. PhysioECG provides functions PQRST waveform delineation computation standard clinical ECG intervals (PR, QT, QTc, QRS duration). vignette demonstrates: Generating synthetic ECG known PQRST morphology R-peak detection entry point morphology analysis PQRST waveform delineation (P-wave, QRS complex, T-wave) Computing clinical ECG intervals QT interval analysis Bazett correction

title: ECG Morphology: PQRST Segmentation and Interval Analysis
code: library(PhysioECG) library(PhysioCore)

title: ECG Morphology: PQRST Segmentation and Interval Analysis
text: make_ecg_pqrst() generator creates synthetic ECG signals physiologically realistic P, Q, R, S, T wave components. also returns data.frame known fiducial points validation. fiducials data.frame includes columns known wave location (r_peak, p_peak, q_point, s_point, t_peak) QRS boundaries (qrs_onset, qrs_offset), sample indices.
code: result <- make_ecg_pqrst(   n_time = 10000,   # 20 seconds at 500 Hz   n_channels = 1,   sr = 500,   heart_rate = 72,   noise_sd = 0.02 )  pe <- result$pe fiducials <- result$fiducials head(fiducials)

title: ECG Morphology: PQRST Segmentation and Interval Analysis
text: Morphology analysis begins R-peak detection. Pan-Tompkins algorithm reliably identifies R-peaks even presence moderate noise. Compare detected peaks known fiducial points:
code: peaks <- ecgDetectRpeaks(pe) head(peaks) # Check detection accuracy n_detected <- nrow(peaks) n_expected <- nrow(fiducials) cat(sprintf("Detected %d peaks, expected %d\n", n_detected, n_expected))

title: ECG Morphology: PQRST Segmentation and Interval Analysis
text: ecgDelineate() function identifies full PQRST complex detected R-peak: QRS onset QRS offset (J-point): detected using gradient-based search R-peak P-wave peak: local maximum 300–80 ms window R-peak T-wave peak: local maximum 80–500 ms window R-peak T-wave end: estimated using tangent-intercept method T-wave downslope result contains one row per beat columns: channel, beat, r_peak, qrs_onset, qrs_offset, qrs_duration_ms, p_peak, t_peak, t_end.
code: delin <- ecgDelineate(pe, peaks) head(delin)

title: ECG Morphology: PQRST Segmentation and Interval Analysis
code: # QRS duration distribution summary(delin$qrs_duration_ms)  # P-wave detection rate p_detected <- sum(!is.na(delin$p_peak)) cat(sprintf("P-wave detected in %d/%d beats (%.0f%%)\n",             p_detected, nrow(delin), 100 * p_detected / nrow(delin)))  # T-wave detection rate t_detected <- sum(!is.na(delin$t_peak)) cat(sprintf("T-wave detected in %d/%d beats (%.0f%%)\n",             t_detected, nrow(delin), 100 * t_detected / nrow(delin)))

title: ECG Morphology: PQRST Segmentation and Interval Analysis
text: using simulated data known fiducial points, can assess delineation accuracy:
code: # Match detected beats to known fiducials by closest R-peak matched <- merge(   delin,   fiducials,   by.x = "beat",   by.y = "beat",   suffixes = c("_detected", "_true") )  # QRS onset accuracy (in samples) onset_error <- matched$qrs_onset - matched$qrs_onset cat(sprintf("QRS onset error: mean = %.1f samples, SD = %.1f samples\n",             mean(onset_error, na.rm = TRUE),             sd(onset_error, na.rm = TRUE)))

title: ECG Morphology: PQRST Segmentation and Interval Analysis
text: ecgIntervals() function calculates standard clinical ECG intervals delineation output: PR interval: P-wave peak QRS onset (ms) QT interval: QRS onset T-wave end (ms) QTc: Corrected QT using Bazett’s formula (QT / sqrt(RR seconds)) QRS duration: QRS onset QRS offset (ms) RR interval: R-peak next R-peak (ms)
code: intervals <- ecgIntervals(delin, sr = samplingRate(pe)) head(intervals)

title: ECG Morphology: PQRST Segmentation and Interval Analysis
text: Normal QRS duration 80–120 ms. Prolonged QRS may indicate bundle branch block ventricular conduction abnormalities.
code: # Summary statistics summary(intervals$qrs_ms)  # Identify beats with prolonged QRS (> 120 ms) prolonged <- intervals[intervals$qrs_ms > 120, ] cat(sprintf("Beats with prolonged QRS: %d/%d\n",             nrow(prolonged), nrow(intervals)))

title: ECG Morphology: PQRST Segmentation and Interval Analysis
text: Normal PR interval 120–200 ms. Shortened PR may indicate pre-excitation (WPW syndrome); prolonged PR suggests first-degree AV block.
code: # Filter beats with detected P-waves pr_valid <- intervals[!is.na(intervals$pr_ms), ] summary(pr_valid$pr_ms)  # Check for PR prolongation pr_prolonged <- pr_valid[pr_valid$pr_ms > 200, ] cat(sprintf("Beats with prolonged PR: %d/%d\n",             nrow(pr_prolonged), nrow(pr_valid)))

title: ECG Morphology: PQRST Segmentation and Interval Analysis
text: QT interval represents ventricular depolarization repolarization. QT varies heart rate, corrected QT (QTc) using Bazett’s formula preferred clinical assessment. Normal QTc 440 ms males 460 ms females.
code: # Filter beats with valid QT measurements qt_valid <- intervals[!is.na(intervals$qt_ms) & !is.na(intervals$qtc_ms), ] summary(qt_valid$qt_ms) summary(qt_valid$qtc_ms)  # Check for QTc prolongation (> 460 ms) qtc_prolonged <- qt_valid[qt_valid$qtc_ms > 460, ] cat(sprintf("Beats with prolonged QTc: %d/%d\n",             nrow(qtc_prolonged), nrow(qt_valid)))

title: ECG Morphology: PQRST Segmentation and Interval Analysis
text: Examine intervals change across beats:
code: # QT variability index if (nrow(qt_valid) > 2) {   qt_sd <- sd(qt_valid$qt_ms, na.rm = TRUE)   rr_sd <- sd(qt_valid$rr_ms, na.rm = TRUE)   cat(sprintf("QT SD: %.1f ms, RR SD: %.1f ms\n", qt_sd, rr_sd)) }

text: delineation interval functions handle multi-channel ECG data. Results computed independently per channel.
code: # Create multi-channel ECG result_mc <- make_ecg_pqrst(n_time = 10000, n_channels = 3, sr = 500) pe_mc <- result_mc$pe  peaks_mc <- ecgDetectRpeaks(pe_mc) delin_mc <- ecgDelineate(pe_mc, peaks_mc) intervals_mc <- ecgIntervals(delin_mc, sr = samplingRate(pe_mc))  # Per-channel summary for (ch in unique(intervals_mc$channel)) {   ch_data <- intervals_mc[intervals_mc$channel == ch, ]   cat(sprintf("Channel %d: %d beats, mean QTc = %.1f ms\n",               ch, nrow(ch_data),               mean(ch_data$qtc_ms, na.rm = TRUE))) }
